term: Cross-industry standard process for data mining
definition: The Cross-industry standard process for data mining, known as CRISP-DM, is an open standard process model that describes common approaches used by data mining experts.
details: It is the most widely-used analytics model. In 2015, IBM released a new methodology called Analytics Solutions Unified Method for Data Mining/Predictive Analytics (also known as ASUM-DM), which refines and extends CRISP-DM.

explainer.lead: CRISP-DM is a shared way of organizing data mining work, built around approaches commonly used by experts. It matters because teams can use the same open standard instead of inventing a separate process for every project.

tiers.eli5: CRISP-DM is like a shared recipe card for data mining projects: it gives experts a common way to organize their work. Anyone can use it because it is an open standard. In 2015, IBM introduced ASUM-DM, which builds on CRISP-DM by refining and extending it.
tiers.practitioner: Use CRISP-DM as a project methodology, not as a mining algorithm or software library. Its open-standard process model gives data mining experts a common way to describe their work and is widely used in analytics. When working with IBM's ASUM-DM, treat it as a 2015 refinement and extension of CRISP-DM rather than the same methodology. A common pitfall is expecting the process model itself to perform the data mining.
tiers.paperLevel: CRISP-DM is formally characterized as an open standard process model describing common approaches used by data mining experts. It is a process methodology rather than a mathematical mining algorithm, and it is described as the most widely used analytics model. IBM released ASUM-DM in 2015 as a methodology that refines and extends CRISP-DM.

explainer.example: A company beginning a customer-analysis data mining project can use CRISP-DM to organize and communicate the work through a standard process model. If the team later adopts IBM's ASUM-DM, it is using a 2015 methodology that refines and extends that foundation.

explainer.intuition: Data mining experts often draw on common approaches, and CRISP-DM packages those approaches into an open standard process model. Its purpose is to provide a shared methodology for the work rather than a particular mining technique.
howItWorks: Start with a data mining project that needs a shared way of working.
Use CRISP-DM as the open standard process model.
Organize and describe the work using common approaches employed by data mining experts.
For a refined and extended methodology, consider IBM's ASUM-DM, released in 2015.
explainer.whyItMatters: CRISP-DM gives data mining and analytics work a common, openly available process model. Its wide use makes it an important reference point, while ASUM-DM shows how the methodology can be refined and extended.
misconceptions: CRISP-DM is not a data mining algorithm; it is a process model.
CRISP-DM is not a proprietary software product; it is an open standard.
ASUM-DM is not simply another name for CRISP-DM; it is an IBM methodology that refines and extends it.
